newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lauds OSCE finding in Serbia vote.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lauds OSCE finding in Serbia vote.

text.p: The United States welcomed on Friday the multilateral confirmation of opposition victories over Serbia's ruling Socialist party in local elections last month.

"The U.S. applauds the work of Former Prime Minister (Felipe) Gonzalez," whose Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe fact-finding panel earlier in the day backed opposition claims that the authorities had cheated them out of victories, the State Department said.

The State Department said the conclusions by Gonzalez, a former Spanish prime minister, "match our own -- that the results of the Nov. 17 elections must be respected, that an open and constructive dialogue between the Milosevic government and the opposition must take place and that Serbia must honour its international commitments and move toward democracy before it can be accepted fully into the international community."

"We call on President (Slobodan) Milosevic to heed the recommendations of the Gonzalez report, and we point out that President Milosevic did agree to the visit by the OSCE delegation," a department spokesman, John Dinger, told reporters.

"We believe that the best way possible to resolve this situation is for President Milosevic to now heed the delegation's recommendations ... that he respect the results of the Nov. 17 elections, that he engage in an open and constructive dialogue with the opposition and that Serbia honour its international commitments to move toward democracy," Dinger added.
